questions.stem: Lisa is attempting to prevent her network from being targeted by IP spoofing attacks as well as preventing her network from being the source of those attacks. Which of the following rules are best practices that Lisa should configure at her network border? (Select all that apply.)
options: Block packets with internal source addresses from entering the network.
Block packets with external source addresses from leaving the network.
Block packets with public IP addresses from entering the network.
Block packets with private IP addresses from exiting the network.
questions.explanation: Packets with public IP addresses will routinely be allowed to enter the network, so you should not create a rule to block them. Packets with internal source addresses should never originate from outside the network, so they should be blocked from entering the network. Packets with external source addresses should never be found on the internal network, so they should be blocked from leaving the network. Finally, private IP addresses should never be used on the Internet, so packets containing private IP addresses should be blocked from leaving the network.
optionNotes: Correct. Traffic arriving from outside should never carry your own internal source addresses. If it does, the address is spoofed, so ingress filtering should drop it.

Correct. Packets from inside your network should never carry an external source address. If they do, someone inside is spoofing, so egress filtering stops your network from being the source of attacks.
Incorrect. Normal, legitimate inbound Internet traffic carries public IP addresses, so blocking it would cut off ordinary communication without addressing spoofing.
Correct. Private (RFC 1918) addresses should never appear on the Internet, so packets with private source addresses should be blocked from leaving the network.

questions.stem: Ed has been tasked with identifying a service that will provide a low-latency, high-performance, and high-availability way to host content for his employer. What type of solution should he seek out to ensure that his employer's customers around the world can access their content quickly, easily, and reliably?
questions.explanation: A content distribution network (CDN) is designed to provide reliable, low-latency, geographically distributed content distribution. In this scenario, a CDN is an ideal solution. A P2P CDN like BitTorrent isn't a typical choice for a commercial entity, whereas redundant servers or a hot site can provide high availability but won't provide the remaining requirements.
optionNotes: Incorrect. A hot site is a fully equipped DR facility that supports availability after a disaster, but it doesn't spread content geographically for low-latency access by customers worldwide.
Correct. A CDN caches and serves content from servers spread across many locations, giving customers around the world reliable, fast, highly available access to it.
Incorrect. Redundant servers add availability, but they don't put content near users around the world, so latency and performance for global customers stay the same.
Incorrect. A P2P CDN such as BitTorrent spreads content through users' peer systems. It isn't a typical choice for a commercial company that needs predictable, reliable delivery.

questions.stem: Fran is building a forensic analysis workstation and is selecting a forensic disk controller to include in the setup. Which of the following are functions of a forensic disk controller? (Select all that apply.)
options: Preventing the modification of data on a storage device
Returning data requested from the device
Reporting errors sent by the device to the forensic host
Blocking read commands sent to the device
questions.explanation: A forensic disk controller performs four functions. One of those, write blocking, intercepts write commands sent to the device and prevents them from modifying data on the device. The other three functions include returning data requested by a read operation, returning access-significant information from the device, and reporting errors from the device back to the forensic host. The controller should not prevent read commands from being sent to the device because those commands may return crucial information.
optionNotes: Correct. Write blocking is one of the controller's four functions. It intercepts write commands so they can't change data on the evidence device.
Correct. The controller passes through read operations and returns the requested data to the forensic host, which is how the analysis gets done.
Correct. Sending the device's error reports back to the forensic host is one of the controller's four defined functions.
Incorrect. The controller blocks writes, not reads. Read commands have to reach the device because they may return crucial evidence.

questions.stem: Mike is building a fault-tolerant server and wants to implement RAID 1. How many physical disks are required to build this solution?
questions.explanation: RAID 1, disk mirroring, requires two physical disks that will contain copies of the same data.
optionNotes: Incorrect. A single disk can't provide fault tolerance. Mirroring needs a second disk to hold a copy of the data, so one disk can't build RAID 1.
Correct. RAID 1 is disk mirroring and needs two physical disks that hold identical copies of the same data.
Incorrect. Three disks is the minimum for RAID 5 (striping with parity), not RAID 1. Mirroring needs only two disks.
Incorrect. Five disks is more than any common RAID level requires as a minimum. RAID 1 mirroring needs just two disks.

questions.stem: Darren is troubleshooting an authentication issue for a Kerberized application used by his organization. He believes the issue is with the generation of session keys. What Kerberos service should he investigate first?
questions.explanation: The TGS, or ticket-granting service (which is usually on the same server as the KDC), receives a TGT from the client. It validates the TGT and the user's rights to access the service they are requesting to use. The TGS then issues a ticket and session keys to the client. The AS serves as the authentication server, which forwards the username to the KDC. It's worth noting that the client doesn't communicate with the KDC directly. Instead, it will communicate with the TGT and the AS, which means KDC isn't an appropriate answer here.
optionNotes: Incorrect. The client doesn't talk to the KDC directly. It works through the AS and the TGS, so the KDC isn't the specific service that issues session keys.
Incorrect. A TGT is a ticket (credential) presented to the TGS, not a Kerberos service, so it cannot be investigated as the session-key-generating service.
Incorrect. The AS authenticates the user and forwards the username to the KDC; it isn't the component that validates TGTs and issues service tickets and session keys.
Correct. The TGS validates the client's TGT and access rights, then issues the service ticket and session keys, so it's the service to check for session key problems.

questions.stem: Evelyn believes that one of her organization's vendors has breached a contractual obligation to protect sensitive data and would like to conduct an investigation into the circumstances. Based upon the results of the investigation, it is likely that Evelyn's organization will sue the vendor for breach of contract. What term best describes the type of investigation that Evelyn is conducting?
questions.explanation: This is an example of a civil investigation because it relates to a contract dispute and will likely wind up being litigated in civil court. Administrative investigations are for internal purposes and are not applicable when a third party is being investigated. Criminal and regulatory investigations may only be initiated by those with regulatory authority, typically government agencies.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Administrative investigations look into internal operational matters, like employee misconduct. They don't fit here because the subject is an outside vendor and the expected result is a lawsuit.

Incorrect. Criminal investigations are opened by government law enforcement into violations of criminal law. A breach of contract is a private dispute, and Evelyn has no authority to bring criminal charges.
Correct. The matter is a contract dispute that will probably be argued in civil court. A civil investigation collects evidence to support a lawsuit against the vendor.

Incorrect. Regulatory investigations are carried out by government agencies or other bodies with regulatory authority. A private organization looking into a vendor's contract performance isn't one of them.

questions.stem: Ivan is installing a motion detector to protect a sensitive work area that uses high-frequency microwave signal transmissions to identify potential intruders. What type of detector is he installing?
questions.explanation: Wave pattern motion detectors transmit ultrasonic or microwave signals into the monitored area, watching for changes in the returned signals bouncing off objects. Infrared heat-based detectors watch for unusual heat patterns. Capacitance detectors work based upon electromagnetic fields.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Infrared detectors look for unusual heat signatures in the monitored area. They don't send out microwave signals, so they don't match the detector described.
Incorrect. Heat-based (infrared) detectors pick up changes in thermal patterns. They don't transmit high-frequency microwave signals and watch the reflections.
Correct. Wave pattern detectors send ultrasonic or microwave signals into the area and watch for changes in the signals that bounce back, which is exactly what Ivan's device does.
Incorrect. Capacitance detectors sense changes in an electromagnetic field around the protected object. They don't transmit microwave signals into the area.

questions.stem: Susan sets up a firewall that keeps track of the status of the communication between two systems and allows a remote system to respond to a local system only after the local system starts communication. What type of firewall is Susan using?
questions.explanation: Stateful packet inspection firewalls, also known as dynamic packet filtering firewalls, track the state of a conversation and can allow a response from a remote system based on an internal system being allowed to start the communication. Static packet filtering and circuit-level gateways only filter based on source and destination IP addresses and ports along with the protocol being used, whereas application-level gateway firewalls proxy traffic for specific applications.
optionNotes: Incorrect. A static packet filter looks at each packet on its own, using source/destination IP, port, and protocol. It has no memory of connection state, so it can't permit replies only to sessions started inside the network.

Incorrect. An application-level gateway proxies traffic for specific applications and inspects it at the application layer. What the question describes is tracking connection state, which is not this firewall's defining feature.

Correct. A stateful packet inspection firewall, also called dynamic packet filtering, tracks the state of each conversation. It lets a remote system reply only after an internal system has started the communication.
Incorrect. A circuit-level gateway filters on addresses, ports, and protocol at session setup. According to the book, it doesn't track conversation state the way a stateful inspection firewall does.

questions.stem:
Scenario:
Ben owns a coffeehouse and wants to provide wireless Internet service for his customers. Ben's network is simple and uses a single consumer-grade wireless router and a cable modem connected via a commercial cable data contract.

How can Ben provide access control for his customers without having to provision user IDs before they connect while also gathering useful contact information for his business purposes?
options: Require customers to use a publicly posted password like “BensCoffee.”
questions.explanation: A captive portal can require those who want to connect to and use Wi-Fi to provide an email address to connect. This allows Ben to provide easy-to-use wireless while meeting his business purposes. WPA2-PSK is the preshared key mode of WPA and won't provide information about users who are given a key. WPA3's SAE mode would be preferable to WPA2-PSK, but it still does not allow for the data gathering Ben desires. Sharing a password doesn't allow for data gathering either.
optionNotes: Incorrect. WPA2-PSK is WPA2's preshared key mode. Every user gets the same key, and Ben learns nothing about who connected, so he collects no contact information.

Correct. A captive portal can ask users for something like an email address before granting access. That gives Ben easy access control with no pre-provisioned accounts, and it collects contact data for his business.
Incorrect. A publicly posted shared password gives only weak access control. It doesn't identify customers or collect any of their contact information.
Incorrect. WPA3 SAE gives better protection than WPA2-PSK, but it's still a password-based way to connect. It doesn't collect customer information the way Ben wants.

questions.stem:
Scenario:
Ben owns a coffeehouse and wants to provide wireless Internet service for his customers. Ben's network is simple and uses a single consumer-grade wireless router and a cable modem connected via a commercial cable data contract.

Ben intends to run an open (unencrypted) wireless network for his customers. How should he connect his wireless business devices?
options: Run WPA3 on the same SSID.
Set up a separate SSID using WPA3.
Run the open network in Enterprise mode.
Set up a separate wireless network using WEP.
questions.explanation: Many modern wireless routers can provide multiple SSIDs. Ben can create a private, secure network for his business operations, but he will need to make sure that the customer and business networks are firewalled or otherwise logically separated from each other. Running WPA3 on the same SSID isn't possible without creating another wireless network and would cause confusion for customers (SSIDs aren't required to be unique). Running a network in Enterprise mode isn't used for open networks, and WEP is outdated and incredibly vulnerable.
optionNotes: Incorrect. A single SSID can't be open and WPA3-protected at once. Doing this would really mean building another wireless network, and customers would get confused because SSIDs don't have to be unique.
Correct. Many modern routers support multiple SSIDs, so Ben can run a private WPA3 network for business devices. He still needs to firewall or logically separate it from the open customer network.
Incorrect. Enterprise mode means 802.1X/RADIUS authentication. It isn't used for open networks, so it doesn't make sense for an unencrypted customer SSID.
Incorrect. A separate network is a good idea, but WEP is an outdated protocol that is extremely easy to break. It would not protect the business devices.

questions.stem:
Scenario:
Ben owns a coffeehouse and wants to provide wireless Internet service for his customers. Ben's network is simple and uses a single consumer-grade wireless router and a cable modem connected via a commercial cable data contract.

After implementing the solution from the first question, Ben receives a complaint about users in his cafe hijacking other customers' web traffic, including using their usernames and passwords. How is this possible?
options: The password is shared by all users, making traffic vulnerable.
A malicious user has installed a Trojan on the router.
A user has ARP spoofed the router, making all traffic broadcast to all users.
Open networks are unencrypted, making traffic easily sniffable.
questions.explanation: Unencrypted open networks broadcast traffic in the clear. This means that unencrypted sessions to websites can be easily captured with a packet sniffer. Some tools like FireSheep have been specifically designed to capture sessions from popular websites. Fortunately, many websites now use TLS by default, but other sites still send user session information in the clear. Shared passwords are not the cause of the vulnerability, ARP spoofing isn't an issue with wireless networks, and a Trojan is designed to look like safe software, not to compromise a router.
optionNotes: Incorrect. An open network uses no password at all, so a shared password can't be the cause. The book says shared passwords are not where this vulnerability comes from.
Incorrect. A Trojan is malware disguised as harmless software that a user installs. It isn't a way to take over a router, and you don't need one to sniff traffic on an open network.
Incorrect. The book says ARP spoofing isn't an issue with wireless networks. On open Wi-Fi, traffic already goes out over the air unencrypted, so no spoofing is needed to capture it.
Correct. Open networks send traffic without encryption, so anyone nearby can use a packet sniffer (or a tool like FireSheep) to capture sessions and credentials from any website that doesn't use TLS.

questions.stem: Kevin is reviewing and updating the security documentation used by his organization. He would like to document some best practices for securing IoT devices that his team has developed over the past year. The practices are generalized in nature and do not cover specific devices. What type of document would be best for this purpose?
questions.explanation: It is possible that Kevin could use any one of these documents. We should zero in on the portion of the question where it indicates that these are best practices. This implies that the advice is not mandatory and, therefore, would not go into a policy or standard. The fact that the advice is general in nature means that it is likely not well-suited to the step-by-step nature of a procedure. A guideline would be the perfect place to document these best practices.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Policies are mandatory, high-level statements of management intent. Kevin's advice is optional best practice, so a policy is the wrong home for it.
Incorrect. Standards set mandatory, specific requirements, such as required configurations. These best practices are not mandatory, so a standard doesn't fit.
Correct. Guidelines hold non-mandatory recommendations and best practices. That matches Kevin's general IoT security advice, which isn't tied to specific devices.
Incorrect. Procedures give detailed step-by-step instructions, usually for a specific task or system. Kevin's advice is general, so it doesn't suit the step-by-step format.

questions.stem: Tom is tuning his security monitoring tools in an attempt to reduce the number of alerts received by administrators without missing important security events. He decides to configure the system to only report failed login attempts if there are five failed attempts to access the same account within a one-hour period of time. What term best describes the technique that Tom is using?
questions.explanation: Clipping is an analysis technique that reports alerts only after they exceed a set threshold. It is a specific form of sampling, which is a more general term that describes any attempt to excerpt records for review. Thresholding is not a commonly used term. Administrators may choose to configure automatic or manual account lockout after failed login attempts, but that is not described in the scenario.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Thresholding is not a commonly used term for this technique. Reporting alerts only after events exceed a set threshold is called clipping.
Incorrect. Sampling is the general term for excerpting any subset of records for review. Clipping is a specific form of sampling, so it is the more precise description of Tom's technique.

Incorrect. Account lockout disables an account after repeated failed logins, which is an access control action. Tom is only filtering which alerts get reported, and nothing in the scenario locks an account.

Correct. Clipping is an analysis technique that raises an alert only after events pass a set threshold, here five failed logins in an hour. It cuts down alert noise without missing significant events.

questions.stem: Sally has been tasked with deploying an authentication, authorization, and accounting server for wireless network services in her organization and needs to avoid using proprietary technology. What technology should she select?
questions.explanation: RADIUS is a common AAA technology used to provide services for dial-up, wireless networks, network devices, and a range of other systems. OAuth is an authorization protocol used to allow applications to act on a user's behalf without sharing the password and is used for many web applications. OpenID Connect is an authentication layer on top of OAuth that allows clients to verify the identity of an end user. XTACACS, an earlier protocol for network authentication, has largely been superseded by more secure and robust protocols like RADIUS, and its proprietary nature does not fit Sally's criteria.
optionNotes: Incorrect. OAuth is an authorization protocol that lets web applications act on a user's behalf without sharing the password. It isn't an AAA server for wireless network access.

Correct. RADIUS is an open, widely used AAA technology. It handles authentication, authorization, and accounting for wireless networks, dial-up access, and network devices, so it fits Sally's requirement to avoid proprietary technology.

Incorrect. XTACACS is an older network authentication protocol that has largely been replaced by more secure options like RADIUS. It's also proprietary (Cisco), which rules it out under Sally's criteria.
Incorrect. OpenID Connect is an authentication layer built on OAuth that lets clients verify a user's identity, mostly for web apps. It doesn't provide AAA services for wireless networks.

questions.stem: An accounting clerk for Christopher's Cheesecakes does not have access to the salary information for individual employees but wanted to know the salary of a new hire. He pulled total payroll expenses for the pay period before the new person was hired and then pulled the same expenses for the following pay period. He computed the difference between those two amounts to determine the individual's salary. What type of attack occurred?
questions.explanation: In an inference attack, the attacker uses several pieces of generic nonsensitive information to determine a specific sensitive value. In a salami slicing attack, the attacker siphons off minute quantities of money many times to accumulate a large amount of funds. In a data diddling attack, the attacker alters the contents of a database. Social engineering attacks exploit human psychology to achieve their goals.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Salami slicing means skimming tiny amounts of money many times until they add up to a large sum. The clerk took no money; he worked out a value he wasn't allowed to see.
Incorrect. Data diddling means changing what's stored in a database. The clerk only read payroll totals and changed nothing.
Correct. This is an inference attack: the clerk combined two pay-period totals he was allowed to see and used the difference to work out one employee's salary, which is sensitive.
Incorrect. Social engineering works by manipulating people's psychology. The clerk didn't trick anyone; he did the arithmetic on data he already had access to.

questions.stem: Alice would like to have read permissions on an object and knows that Bob already has those rights and would like to give them to herself. Which one of the rules in the Take-Grant protection model would allow her to complete this operation if the relationship exists between Alice and Bob?
questions.explanation: The Take rule in the Take-Grant protection model allows a subject to take rights from another object if the subject has the take right over that object. In this scenario, if Alice has the take right over Bob and Bob has read permissions on an object, Alice can use the Take rule to grant herself the read permissions that Bob possesses. The Grant rule is for granting rights to other subjects, not for taking them for oneself. The Create rule is used to create new objects or rights, not to transfer existing ones. There is no Remote rule in the Take-Grant protection model.
optionNotes: Correct. The Take rule lets a subject with the take right over another subject (Bob) acquire that subject's rights, so Alice can give herself Bob's read permission.
Incorrect. The Grant rule lets a subject pass its own rights to someone else. Here Alice wants to acquire Bob's rights herself, so Grant doesn't describe what she's doing.
Incorrect. The Create rule lets a subject create new objects or rights. It doesn't move existing rights from Bob to Alice.
Incorrect. Take-Grant has no Remote rule. Its rules are take, grant, create and remove.

questions.stem:
During a log review, Danielle discovers a series of logs that show login failures: Jan 31 11:39:12 ip-10-0-0-2 sshd[29092]: Invalid user admin from remotehost passwd=aaaaaaaa Jan 31 11:39:20 ip-10-0-0-2 sshd[29098]: Invalid user admin from remotehost passwd=aaaaaaab Jan 31 11:39:23 ip-10-0-0-2 sshd[29100]: Invalid user admin from remotehost passwd=aaaaaaac Jan 31 11:39:31 ip-10-0-0-2 sshd[29106]: Invalid user admin from remotehost passwd=aaaaaaad Jan 31 20:40:53 ip-10-0-0-2 sshd[30520]: Invalid user admin from remotehost passwd=aaaaaaae
What type of attack has Danielle discovered?
questions.explanation: Brute-force attacks try every possible password. In this attack, the password is changing by one letter at each attempt, which indicates that it is a brute-force attack. A dictionary attack would use dictionary words for the attack, whereas a man-in-the-middle or pass-the-hash attack would most likely not be visible in an authentication log except as a successful login.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Pass-the-hash reuses a stolen password hash to authenticate. It wouldn't produce a run of failed guesses; at most it would show up in the log as one successful login.
Correct. Each attempt changes the password by one character (aaaaaaaa, aaaaaaab, aaaaaaac...). That is a brute-force attack working through every possible combination in order.

Incorrect. A man-in-the-middle attack intercepts or relays traffic between two parties. It wouldn't create a series of failed SSH logins with incrementing passwords, and would probably appear only as a successful login.
Incorrect. A dictionary attack tries real words or common passwords from a list. Strings like 'aaaaaaab' aren't dictionary words; they come from stepping through every combination.

questions.stem: Ben is designing a database-driven application and would like to ensure that two executing transactions do not affect each other by storing interim results in the database. What property is he seeking to enforce?
questions.explanation: Isolation requires that transactions operate separately from each other. Atomicity ensures that if any part of a database transaction fails, the entire transaction must be rolled back as if it never occurred. Consistency ensures that all transactions are consistent with the logical rules of the database, such as having a primary key. Durability requires that once a transaction is committed to the database it must be preserved. Together, these properties make up the ACID model.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Atomicity is the all-or-nothing rule: if any part of a transaction fails, the whole transaction is rolled back. It says nothing about keeping concurrent transactions apart.
Correct. Isolation requires transactions to run separately, so one transaction never sees or depends on another transaction's interim, uncommitted results.
Incorrect. Consistency means every transaction follows the database's logical rules, such as primary key constraints. It doesn't stop concurrent transactions from interfering with each other.
Incorrect. Durability means a committed transaction stays saved, even after a failure. It deals with persistence, not with separating transactions that run at the same time.

questions.stem: Kim is the system administrator for a small business network that is experiencing security problems. She is in the office in the evening working on the problem, and nobody else is there. As she is watching, she can see that systems on the other side of the office that were previously behaving normally are now exhibiting signs of an infection one after the other. What type of malware is Kim likely dealing with?
questions.explanation: Worms have built-in propagation mechanisms that do not require user interaction, such as scanning for systems containing known vulnerabilities and then exploiting those vulnerabilities to gain access. Viruses and Trojan horses typically require user interaction to spread. Logic bombs do not spread from system to system but lie in wait until certain conditions are met, triggering the delivery of their payload.
optionNotes: Incorrect. A virus usually needs a user to do something, like opening a file or running a program, before it spreads. Nobody else is in the office, so a virus can't account for machines getting infected one after another.
Correct. Worms spread by themselves, with no user involved. They scan for vulnerable systems and exploit them, so machines in an empty office get infected one after another.
Incorrect. A Trojan horse pretends to be legitimate software, and a user has to install or run it. Without users present, it can't explain the infection jumping from system to system.
Incorrect. A logic bomb doesn't move between systems. It sits on one host until a trigger condition is met and then delivers its payload, so it doesn't fit infections spreading across machines.

questions.stem: Barb is reviewing the compliance obligations facing her organization and the types of liability that each one might incur. Which of the following laws and regulations may involve criminal penalties if violated? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: The Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) is a U.S. law governing the healthcare sector that does provide for criminal penalties. The Sarbanes–Oxley (SOX) Act governs publicly traded corporations and also provides for criminal penalties. The Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA) is a U.S. law governing educational records, but it does not provide for criminal penalties. PCI DSS, the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard, is an industry standard for payment card operations and handling. Because it is not a law, PCI DSS violations cannot incur criminal sanctions.
optionNotes: Incorrect. FERPA protects the privacy of student educational records. It is a U.S. law, but it has no criminal penalties. Its main enforcement tool is pulling federal funding from institutions.
Correct. HIPAA is a U.S. law covering healthcare privacy and security, and it does provide criminal penalties for certain violations, such as knowingly misusing protected health information.
Correct. SOX governs publicly traded corporations and includes criminal penalties, for example against executives who knowingly certify false financial reports.
Incorrect. PCI DSS is a payment card industry standard enforced through contracts, not a law. Breaking it can bring fines or loss of card-processing privileges, but never criminal sanctions.

questions.stem: Quentin is analyzing network traffic that he collected with Wireshark on a TCP/IP network. He would like to identify all new connections that were set up during his traffic collection. If he is looking for the three packets that constitute the TCP three-way handshake used to establish a new connection, what flags should be set on the first three packets?
questions.explanation: The TCP three-way handshake consists of an initial contact via a SYN, or synchronize flagged packet, which receives a response with a SYN/ACK, or synchronize and acknowledge flagged packet, which is acknowledged by the original sender with an ACK, or acknowledge packet. RST is used in TCP to reset a connection, PSH is used to send data immediately, and FIN is used to end a connection.
optionNotes: Incorrect. The flags are right but the order is wrong. The server's SYN/ACK reply has to come before the client's final ACK, so ACK can't be the second packet.
Incorrect. None of these flags opens a connection. PSH tells the receiver to deliver data immediately, RST resets a connection, and ACK only acknowledges. There's no SYN to start the session.
Correct. The client sends a SYN, the server answers with a SYN/ACK, and the client confirms with an ACK. That completes the three-way handshake.
Incorrect. SYN does start the handshake, but RST resets a connection and FIN closes one. Neither is part of setting up a new session.

questions.stem: Daniel is selecting a mobile device management (MDM) solution for his organization and is writing the RFP. He is trying to decide what features he should include as requirements after aligning his organization's security needs with an MDM platform's capabilities. Which of the following are typical capabilities of MDM solutions? (Select all that apply.)
options: Remotely wiping the contents of a mobile device
Assuming control of a nonregistered BYOD mobile device
Enforcing the use of device encryption
questions.explanation: MDM products do not have the capability of assuming control of a device not currently managed by the organization. This would be equivalent to hacking into a device owned by someone else and might constitute a crime. They do normally provide the ability to manage device backups, enforce the use of encryption, and remotely wipe the contents of mobile devices.
optionNotes: Correct. A standard MDM feature is remote wipe, which erases a lost or stolen managed device so its data isn't exposed.
Incorrect. MDM can only manage devices enrolled with the organization. Taking control of an unregistered personal device would amount to hacking someone else's device and could be a crime.
Correct. MDM platforms usually let administrators set policies that require device encryption on managed devices.
Correct. MDM solutions normally include managing device backups, so data on managed devices can be recovered.

questions.stem: Jim is implementing an IDaaS solution for his organization. What type of technology is he putting in place?
questions.explanation: Identity as a service (IDaaS) provides an identity platform as a third-party service. This can provide benefits, including integration with cloud services and removing overhead for maintenance of traditional on-premises identity systems but can also create risk due to third-party control of identity services and reliance on an off-site identity infrastructure.
optionNotes: Correct. IDaaS stands for identity as a service: a third-party, often cloud-hosted identity platform. It integrates with cloud services and removes on-premises maintenance, but it makes the organization dependent on an outside provider.
Incorrect. "Employee ID as a service" is not a real service category. The "ID" in IDaaS refers to identity management in general (authentication, provisioning, SSO), not employee ID numbers.

Incorrect. In IDaaS, "ID" means identity, not intrusion detection. An IDS is a detective control that monitors traffic for suspicious activity, which is different from a third-party identity platform.

Incorrect. OAuth is an authorization framework that lets users grant delegated access to resources. An IDaaS platform may support it, but OAuth is a protocol, not the hosted identity service the acronym describes.

questions.stem: Gina recently took the CISSP certification exam and then wrote a blog post that included the text of many of the exam questions that she experienced. What aspect of the ISC2 Code of Ethics is most directly violated in this situation?
options: Act honorably, honestly, justly, responsibly, and legally.
Protect society, the common good, necessary public trust and confidence, and the infrastructure.
Provide diligent and competent service to principals.
questions.explanation: Gina's actions harm the CISSP certification and information security community by undermining the integrity of the examination process. While Gina also is acting dishonestly, the harm to the profession is more of a direct violation of the ISC2 Code of Ethics.
optionNotes: Correct. Posting live exam questions breaks the integrity of the CISSP exam process and devalues the credential, which directly harms the profession and the security community.
Incorrect. Gina is being dishonest, and that does break this second canon. But the book says the harm to the profession is the more direct violation, so this is not the best answer.

Incorrect. This first canon is about protecting society, public trust and infrastructure. Leaking exam content mostly damages the certification and the profession, not society or the infrastructure at large.

Incorrect. This third canon is about giving diligent, competent service to principals such as employers and clients. No principal relationship is involved when someone posts exam questions on a personal blog.

questions.stem: Gordon is conducting a risk assessment for his organization and determined the amount of damage that flooding is expected to cause to his facilities each year. What metric has Gordon identified?
questions.explanation: The annualized loss expectancy (ALE) is the amount of damage that the organization expects to occur each year as the result of a given risk. ALE is calculated by multiplying the single loss expectancy (SLE), which is the expected financial loss from a single flooding event, by the annual rate of occurrence (ARO), which is the expected frequency of flooding events per year. The ALE helps organizations to understand the potential impact of risks and to make informed decisions about risk mitigation strategies and investments in protective measures. The exposure factor (EF) is the percentage of the asset expected to be damaged during an incident.
optionNotes: Correct. ALE is the expected yearly loss from a given risk, here flooding damage per year. It's calculated as SLE × ARO.
Incorrect. ARO is how often flooding is expected to happen each year. It measures frequency, not a damage amount.
Incorrect. SLE is the expected financial loss from one flooding event. It is not the loss expected over a whole year.
Incorrect. EF is the percentage of an asset expected to be damaged in one incident. It is not a yearly damage figure.

questions.stem: Greg would like to implement application control technology in his organization. He would like to limit users to installing only approved software on their systems. What type of application control would be appropriate in this situation?
questions.explanation: The whitelisting approach to application control allows users to install only those software packages specifically approved by administrators. This would be an appropriate approach in a scenario where application installation needs to be tightly controlled. Blacklisting, which blocks known malicious or unauthorized applications, would not be as effective in this scenario because it allows all software to run unless it appears on the blacklist. Graylisting and bluelisting are made-up terms.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Blacklisting blocks only known malicious or unauthorized applications and lets everything else run, so it can't restrict users to approved software only.
Incorrect. Graylisting isn't a real application control approach. The book treats it as a made-up term in this context.
Correct. Whitelisting lets users install only the software that administrators have specifically approved. That gives the tight control over installations that Greg wants.
Incorrect. Bluelisting is a made-up term, not a real type of application control.

questions.stem: Frank is the security administrator for a web server that provides news and information to people located around the world. His server received an unusually high volume of traffic that it could not handle and was forced to reject requests. Frank traced the source of the traffic back to a botnet. What type of attack took place?
questions.explanation: This is a clear example of a denial-of-service attack—denying legitimate users authorized access to the system through the use of overwhelming traffic. It goes beyond a reconnaissance attack because the attacker is affecting the system, but it is not a compromise because the attacker did not attempt to gain access to the system. There is no reason to believe that a malicious insider was involved.
optionNotes: Correct. The botnet flooded the server with so much traffic that it had to reject requests, which kept legitimate users from reaching it. That is the definition of a (distributed) denial-of-service attack.
Incorrect. Reconnaissance only gathers information about a target, such as by scanning or probing. Here the attacker actually hurt the system's availability, so it goes beyond reconnaissance.
Incorrect. A compromise means an attacker gains unauthorized access to the system. The botnet only overloaded the server and made no attempt to get access.
Incorrect. The traffic came from an external botnet, and nothing points to an employee or other trusted insider being involved.

questions.stem:
In the database table shown here, which column would be the best candidate for a primary key?
[Exhibit, transcribed from the book's figure:]
Company ID | Company Name | Address | City | State | ZIP Code | Telephone | Sales Rep
1 | Acme Widgets | 234 Main Street | Columbia | MD | 21040 | (301) 555-1212 | 14
2 | Abrams Consulting | 1024 Sample Street | Miami | FL | 33131 | (305) 555-1995 | 14
3 | Dome Widgets | 913 Sorin Street | South Bend | IN | 46556 | (574) 555-5863 | 26
questions.explanation: The Company ID column is likely unique for each row in the table, making it the best choice for a primary key. There may be multiple companies that share the same name or ZIP code. Similarly, a single sales representative likely serves more than one company, making those fields unsuitable for use as a unique identifier.
optionNotes: Correct. Company ID is a surrogate identifier that is probably unique for every row, so it's the best primary key candidate.
Incorrect. Different companies can have the same name, so Company Name isn't guaranteed to identify a row uniquely and makes a poor primary key.
Incorrect. Many companies can be in the same ZIP code, so its values can repeat across rows and can't serve as a unique identifier.
Incorrect. One sales rep usually serves several customers, and rep 14 already appears twice here. That makes Sales Rep a foreign key that points to the Sales Reps table, not a unique primary key.

questions.stem: Gwen is a cybersecurity professional for a financial services firm that maintains records of their customers. These records include personal information about each customer, including the customer's name, Social Security number, date and place of birth, and mother's maiden name. What category best describes these records?
questions.explanation: Personally identifiable information (PII) includes data that can be used to distinguish or trace that person's identity and also includes their educational, financial, and employment information. PHI is personal health information, EDI is electronic data interchange, and proprietary data is used to maintain an organization's competitive advantage.
optionNotes: Incorrect. PHI is protected health information, such as medical records and treatment data. These records hold identity details, not health data, so PHI doesn't fit.
Incorrect. Proprietary data is information an organization protects to keep its competitive advantage, like trade secrets. Customer identity records aren't in that category.
Correct. Name, SSN, date and place of birth, and mother's maiden name can each be used to identify or trace a specific person, which makes them personally identifiable information.
Incorrect. EDI (electronic data interchange) is a standard for exchanging business documents electronically between organizations. It's a transfer method, not a type of personal data.

questions.stem: Bob is configuring egress filtering on his network, examining traffic destined for the Internet. His organization uses the public address range 12.8.195.0/24. Packets with which one of the following destination addresses should Bob permit to leave the network?
questions.explanation: 129.53.44.124 is a valid public IP address and a legitimate destination for traffic leaving Bob's network. 12.8.195.15 is a public address on Bob's network and should not be a destination address on a packet leaving the network. 10.8.15.9 and 192.168.109.55 are both private IP addresses that should not be routed to the Internet.
optionNotes: Incorrect. 12.8.195.15 sits inside Bob's own 12.8.195.0/24 range. Traffic addressed to his own network shouldn't be headed out to the Internet, so egress filtering should block it.
Incorrect. 10.8.15.9 is in the RFC 1918 private block 10.0.0.0/8. Private addresses can't be routed on the Internet, so packets addressed to them shouldn't leave the network.
Incorrect. 192.168.109.55 is in the RFC 1918 private block 192.168.0.0/16. It can't be routed on the Internet, so egress filtering should drop packets addressed to it.
Correct. 129.53.44.124 is a valid public address outside Bob's range, which makes it a legitimate Internet destination for outbound traffic.

questions.stem: Brian is considering increasing the length of the cryptographic keys used by his organization. If he adds 8 bits to the encryption key, how many more possible keys will be added to the keyspace for the algorithm?
options: The size of the keyspace will double.
The size of the keyspace will increase by a factor of 8.
The size of the keyspace will increase by a factor of 64.
The size of the keyspace will increase by a factor of 256.
questions.explanation: Binary keyspaces contain a number of keys equal to 2 raised to the power of the number of bits. Two to the eighth power is 256, so the keyspace will increase by a factor of 256.
optionNotes: Incorrect. The keyspace doubles only when you add a single bit (2^1 = 2). Adding 8 bits multiplies it by 2^8, not by 2.
Incorrect. This treats extra bits as if they add keys in a straight line. Each added bit doubles the keyspace, so 8 bits multiply it by 2^8 = 256, not by 8.
Incorrect. 64 is 8 squared, or 2^6, and comes from a miscalculation. The correct factor for 8 more bits is 2^8 = 256.
Correct. A binary keyspace holds 2^n keys, so adding 8 bits multiplies the number of possible keys by 2^8 = 256.

questions.stem: GAD Systems is concerned about the risk of hackers stealing sensitive information stored on a file server. They choose to pursue a risk mitigation strategy. Which one of the following actions would support that strategy?
questions.explanation: Encrypting the files reduces the probability that the data will be successfully stolen, so it is an example of risk mitigation. Deleting the files would be risk avoidance. Purchasing insurance would be risk transference. Taking no action would be risk acceptance.
optionNotes: Correct. Encryption is a control that lowers the chance the stolen data can actually be used, which reduces the risk. That makes it risk mitigation.
Incorrect. Deleting the files gets rid of the risky asset altogether. That is risk avoidance, not mitigation.
Incorrect. Cyber-liability insurance moves the financial impact to the insurer. That is risk transference, and it does nothing to make theft less likely.
Incorrect. Doing nothing means knowingly living with the risk. That is risk acceptance, not mitigation.

questions.stem: Viola is conducting a user account audit to determine whether accounts have the appropriate level of permissions and that all permissions were approved through a formal process. The organization has approximately 50,000 user accounts and an annual employee turnover rate of 24%. Which one of the following sampling approaches would be the most effective use of her time when choosing records for manual review?
options: Select all records that have been modified during the past month.
Ask access administrators to identify the accounts most likely to have issues and audit those.
Select a random sample of records, either from the entire population or from the population of records that have changed during the audit period.
Sampling is not effective in this situation, and all accounts should be audited.
questions.explanation: Sampling should be done randomly to avoid human bias. Sampling is an effective process if it is done on a truly random sample of sufficient size to provide effective coverage of the userbase. It is infeasible for a single person to review every single record. In an organization of 50,000 users with a 24% annual turnover, it is likely that at least 1,000 of those records have changed in the last month. This is still too many records to review. Asking account administrators to select the records to review is a conflict of interest, as they are the group being audited.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Taking every record changed in the past month isn't a sample. With 50,000 users and 24% turnover, that is likely more than 1,000 records, which is still too many for one person to review by hand.
Incorrect. Letting access administrators pick the accounts is a conflict of interest, because they are the group being audited. It also brings human bias into the selection.

Correct. A random sample of sufficient size avoids human bias and gives effective coverage of the user base. Drawing it from the whole population or from the records changed in the period keeps the review manageable.
Incorrect. Sampling works here if it is truly random and large enough. One person can't feasibly review all 50,000 records by hand.

questions.stem: Lila is reviewing her organization's adverse termination process. In that process, when would be the most appropriate time to revoke a user's access privileges to digital systems?
options: At the time the user is informed of the termination
At the end of the last day of employment
At the time the decision is made
Several days after the last day of employment
questions.explanation: In the case of an involuntary termination under adverse circumstances, the user is being fired and may have a negative and potentially hostile reaction. For this reason, it is important to terminate access immediately upon the user being informed of the termination. Terminating access prior to notification may tip the user off to the termination in advance. Leaving access privileges available after termination poses a risk of malicious insider activity.
optionNotes: Correct. Revoking access the moment the user is told about the firing keeps a possibly hostile employee from doing damage, and it doesn't warn them ahead of time.
Incorrect. Under adverse circumstances, waiting until the end of the last day leaves a fired and possibly angry user with access after being told. That opens a window for malicious insider activity.
Incorrect. The decision may come well before the user is told. Cutting access at that point could tip the user off to the termination in advance.
Incorrect. Leaving privileges active for days after employment ends creates serious insider and orphaned-account risk. Access should be removed right away, not later.

questions.stem:
William is reviewing log files that were stored on a system with a suspected compromise. He finds the log file shown here. What type of log file is this?
[Exhibit, transcribed from the book's figure:]
217.69.133.190 - - [11/Apr/2016:09:41:48 -0400] "GET /forum/viewtopic.php?f=4&t=25630 HTTP/1.1" 503 2009 "-" "Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; Linux x86_64; Mail.RU_Bot/2.0; +http://go.mail.ru/help/robots)"
188.143.234.155 - - [11/Apr/2016:09:41:50 -0400] "GET /ask-a-pci-dss-question/ HTTP/1.1" 200 6501 "-" "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 6.1; WOW64; rv:41.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/41.0"
217.69.133.242 - - [11/Apr/2016:09:41:51 -0400] "GET /forum/viewtopic.php?f=5&t=27086 HTTP/1.1" 503 2009 "-" "Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; Linux x86_64; Mail.RU_Bot/2.0; +http://go.mail.ru/help/robots)"
217.69.133.245 - - [11/Apr/2016:09:41:59 -0400] "GET /pci-dss/pci-dss-vulnerability-scanning-requirements/ HTTP/1.1" 301 - "-" "Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; Linux x86_64; Mail.RU_Bot/2.0; +http://go.mail.ru/help/robots)"
[…more lines of the same form…]
207.46.13.18 - - [11/Apr/2016:09:42:17 -0400] "GET /category/articles/page/3/ HTTP/1.1" 200 7583 "-" "Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; bingbot/2.0; +http://www.bing.com/bingbot.htm)"
questions.explanation: The file clearly shows HTTP requests, as evidenced by the many GET commands. Therefore, this is an example of an application log from an HTTP server.
optionNotes: Incorrect. A firewall log records allowed and denied connections: source and destination IPs, ports, protocols, and rule actions. These entries show HTTP GET requests, status codes, and user agents, which a web server writes, not a firewall.
Incorrect. A change log tracks change requests, approvals, and the changes actually made to a system as part of change management. These lines are web page requests, not change records.
Correct. The many GET commands, HTTP status codes, and browser/bot user agents show this is an HTTP server's access log, which is an application log.
Incorrect. A system log records operating system events such as startup and shutdown, service failures, and driver errors. It doesn't record individual HTTP requests made to a web application.

questions.stem: Roger is reviewing a list of security vulnerabilities in his organization and rating them based upon their severity. Which one of the following models would be most useful to his work?
questions.explanation: The Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) is a standardized approach to rating the severity of vulnerabilities and would be the most helpful tool for Roger's work. The STRIDE and ATT&CK models are used to classify the nature, not the severity, of threats. The PASTA model is designed to help with countermeasure selection.
optionNotes: Correct. CVSS is the standardized system for scoring vulnerability severity (0–10). That makes it the right fit for Roger, who is rating vulnerabilities by how severe they are.
Incorrect. STRIDE is a threat-modeling scheme that sorts threats by type (spoofing, tampering, and so on). It describes what kind of threat something is, not how severe a vulnerability is.
Incorrect. PASTA is a seven-stage, risk-centric threat-modeling method meant to help choose countermeasures. It doesn't score individual vulnerabilities by severity.
Incorrect. MITRE ATT&CK is a knowledge base of adversary tactics and techniques. It classifies how attacks work, not how severe a vulnerability is.

questions.stem: An attacker recently called an organization's help desk and persuaded them to reset a password for another user's account. What term best describes this attack?
questions.explanation: Social engineering exploits humans to allow attacks to succeed. Since help-desk employees are specifically tasked with being helpful, they may be targeted by attackers posing as legitimate employees. Trojans are a type of malware, whereas phishing is a targeted attack via electronic communication methods intended to capture passwords or other sensitive data. Whaling is a type of phishing aimed at high-profile or important targets.
optionNotes: Incorrect. "Human Trojan" isn't a standard attack term. A Trojan is malware disguised as legitimate software, and nothing in this phone call to the help desk involved malicious code.

Correct. Social engineering manipulates people into helping an attack succeed. Help-desk staff are paid to be helpful, which makes them easy targets for an attacker pretending to be a real employee who needs a password reset.

Incorrect. Phishing is carried out through electronic messages, such as email, to steal passwords or other sensitive data. This attack was a phone call that persuaded staff to reset a password, so the broader term social engineering fits better.
Incorrect. Whaling is a kind of phishing aimed at high-profile targets such as executives. Here the person deceived was a help-desk employee, and the attack came by phone rather than by email.

questions.stem: Greg is evaluating a new vendor that will be supplying networking gear to his organization. Because of the nature of his organization's work, Greg is concerned that an attacker might attempt a supply chain exploit. Assuming that both Greg's organization and the vendor operate under reasonable security procedures, which one of the following activities likely poses the greatest supply chain risk to the equipment?
options: Tampering by an unauthorized third party at the vendor's site
Misconfiguration by an administrator after installation
Tampering by an unauthorized third party at Greg's site
questions.explanation: If the vendor operates with reasonable security procedures, it is unlikely that the devices will be tampered with at the vendor's site. Similarly, if Greg's organization has reasonable security procedures, tampering at his site is also unlikely. Misconfiguration by an administrator is always possible, but this is a post-installation risk and not a supply chain risk. It is possible that devices will be intercepted and tampered with while in transit from the vendor to Greg's organization.
optionNotes: Incorrect. The question assumes the vendor follows reasonable security procedures, so an unauthorized third party tampering with gear at the vendor's site is unlikely. It is not the biggest risk here.
Correct. Once the devices leave the vendor's site and before they reach Greg's, neither side's security controls protect them. That gap is when interception and tampering in transit is most likely.
Incorrect. An administrator misconfiguring the gear is always possible, but it happens after installation. It is an operational risk, not a supply chain risk.
Incorrect. The question assumes Greg's organization also has reasonable security procedures, so tampering after delivery to his site is unlikely.

questions.stem: Kevin is operating in a single-level security environment and is seeking to classify information systems according to the type of information that they process. What procedure would be the best way for him to assign asset classifications?
options: Assign systems the classification of information that they most commonly process.
Assign systems the classification of the highest level of information that they are expected to process regularly.
Assign systems the classification of the highest level of information that they are ever expected to process.
Assign all systems the same classification level.
questions.explanation: In a single-level security environment, systems should be assigned the classification level of the highest classification of information they are ever expected to process. Systems may not process information that is above their classification level without reclassifying the system upward.
optionNotes: Incorrect. If the system takes its classification from what it processes most often, any less frequent higher-level data would sit on an underclassified system. A single-level system must instead be rated for the highest level it will ever handle.

Incorrect. Looking only at data processed regularly ignores occasional higher-level data. The system would then handle information above its classification, which isn't allowed unless the system is first reclassified upward.

Correct. In a single-level environment, a system is classified at the highest level of information it is ever expected to process. It can't process anything above that level without first being reclassified upward.

Incorrect. A single classification for every system ignores what each system actually processes. Systems holding sensitive data would be underprotected, or low-risk systems would be overprotected, which defeats the purpose of classifying assets by their data.

questions.stem:
Scenario:
The organization that Ben works for has a traditional on-site Active Directory environment that uses a manual provisioning process for each addition to their 350-employee company. As the company adopts new technologies, they are increasingly using software-as-a-service applications to replace their internally developed software stack. Ben has been tasked with designing an identity management implementation that will allow his company to use cloud services while supporting their existing systems. Using the logical diagram shown here, answer the following questions about the identity recommendations Ben should make.
[Figure, described in text: a corporate internal network (employee workstations, Active Directory, CRM, database) connects through a corporate secure border to the Internet, where a business partner and a cloud eCommerce application are also connected.]

If availability of authentication services is the organization's biggest priority, what type of identity platform should Ben recommend?
questions.explanation: A hybrid authentication service can provide authentication services both in the cloud and on-premises, ensuring that service outages due to interrupted links are minimized. An on-site service would continue to work during an Internet outage but would not allow the e-commerce website to authenticate. A cloud service would leave the corporate location offline. Outsourcing authentication does not indicate whether the solution is on- or off-premises and thus isn't a useful answer.
optionNotes: Incorrect. An on-site identity platform keeps internal authentication running during an Internet outage, but the cloud e-commerce application could no longer authenticate users, so availability is only partial.
Incorrect. With a purely cloud-based platform, the corporate location can't authenticate if the Internet link goes down. Availability depends entirely on the link and the provider.
Correct. A hybrid platform provides authentication both on-premises and in the cloud, so an interrupted link doesn't take down either environment's authentication. This maximizes availability.
Incorrect. Outsourcing only says who runs the service, not whether it is on-premises or off-premises. It doesn't address where authentication is available, so it isn't a useful answer.

questions.stem:
Scenario:
The organization that Ben works for has a traditional on-site Active Directory environment that uses a manual provisioning process for each addition to their 350-employee company. As the company adopts new technologies, they are increasingly using software-as-a-service applications to replace their internally developed software stack. Ben has been tasked with designing an identity management implementation that will allow his company to use cloud services while supporting their existing systems. Using the logical diagram shown here, answer the following questions about the identity recommendations Ben should make.
[Figure, described in text: a corporate internal network (employee workstations, Active Directory, CRM, database) connects through a corporate secure border to the Internet, where a business partner and a cloud eCommerce application are also connected.]

If Ben needs to share identity information with the business partner shown, what should he investigate?
questions.explanation: Federation links identity information between multiple organizations. Federating with a business partner can allow identification and authorization to occur between them, making integration much easier. Single sign-on would reduce the number of times a user has to log in but will not facilitate the sharing of identity information. Multifactor authentication can help secure authentication but again doesn't help integrate with a third party. Finally, an identity as a service provider might provide federation but doesn't guarantee it.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Single sign-on cuts down how often users have to log in, but on its own it doesn't share identity information with an outside organization like the business partner.
Incorrect. Multifactor authentication makes authentication stronger. It doesn't connect or share identity data with a third-party partner.
Correct. Federation links identity information across separate organizations, so identification and authorization can happen between Ben's company and the business partner.
Incorrect. IDaaS is a cloud-hosted identity and access management service. A provider may offer federation, but using IDaaS doesn't guarantee identities can be shared with the partner.

questions.stem:
Scenario:
The organization that Ben works for has a traditional on-site Active Directory environment that uses a manual provisioning process for each addition to their 350-employee company. As the company adopts new technologies, they are increasingly using software-as-a-service applications to replace their internally developed software stack. Ben has been tasked with designing an identity management implementation that will allow his company to use cloud services while supporting their existing systems. Using the logical diagram shown here, answer the following questions about the identity recommendations Ben should make.
[Figure, described in text: a corporate internal network (employee workstations, Active Directory, CRM, database) connects through a corporate secure border to the Internet, where a business partner and a cloud eCommerce application are also connected.]

What technology is likely to be involved when Ben's organization needs to provide authentication and authorization assertions to their cloud e-commerce application?
questions.explanation: Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) is frequently used to integrate cloud services and provides the ability to make authentication and authorization assertions. Active Directory integrations are possible but are less common for cloud service providers, and RADIUS is not typically used for integrations like this. Service Provisioning Markup Language (SPML) is used to provision users, resources, and services, not for authentication and authorization.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Active Directory is the on-site directory service. It can integrate with cloud services, but cloud providers rarely use it directly to receive authentication and authorization assertions.

Correct. SAML is an XML-based standard that is widely used to integrate cloud services. It lets the identity provider send authentication and authorization assertions to service providers such as the cloud e-commerce application.
Incorrect. RADIUS is a centralized AAA protocol, typically used for network access such as VPNs and Wi-Fi. It isn't normally used to send identity assertions to SaaS applications.
Incorrect. SPML is used to provision users, resources and services, for example to replace the manual account-creation process. It does not make authentication or authorization assertions.

questions.stem: Dave is responsible for password security in his organization and would like to strengthen the security of password files. He would like to defend his organization against the use of rainbow tables. Which one of the following techniques is specifically designed to frustrate the use of rainbow tables?
questions.explanation: Rainbow tables use precomputed password hashes to conduct cracking attacks against password files. They may be frustrated by the use of salting, which adds a specified value to the password prior to hashing, making it much more difficult to perform precomputation. Password expiration policies, password complexity policies, and user education may all contribute to password security, but they are not direct defenses against the use of rainbow tables.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Expiration policies force periodic password changes, which helps general password security, but they don't stop an attacker from looking up stolen unsalted hashes in a precomputed rainbow table.

Correct. Salting adds a unique value to each password before it is hashed. This makes the precomputed hashes in a rainbow table useless, because an attacker would need a separate table for every salt.
Incorrect. Teaching users good password habits strengthens password security overall, but it's a human-focused control and isn't a direct technical defense against rainbow table lookups.
Incorrect. Complexity rules make passwords harder to guess, but they aren't a direct defense against rainbow tables. Unsalted hashes of complex passwords can still be precomputed in a table.

questions.stem: Helen recently built a new system as part of her organization's deception campaign. The system is configured in a manner that makes it vulnerable to attack and that conveys that it might contain highly sensitive information. What term best describes this system?
questions.explanation: A honeypot is a decoy computer system used to bait intruders into attacking. A honeynet is a network of multiple honeypots that creates a more sophisticated environment for intruders to explore. A pseudoflaw is a false vulnerability in a system that may attract an attacker. A darknet is a segment of unused network address space that should have no network activity and, therefore, may be easily used to monitor for illicit activity.
optionNotes: Incorrect. A honeynet is a network of several honeypots that gives intruders a richer environment to explore. Helen built one decoy system, not a network of them.
Incorrect. A darknet is a block of unused address space that should see no traffic, so any activity there is a sign of something illicit. It is not a single decoy system made to look attractive.
Correct. A honeypot is a single decoy computer that is deliberately left vulnerable and made to look valuable so that it baits intruders into attacking it.
Incorrect. A pseudoflaw is one fake vulnerability placed inside a system to attract attackers. Helen built a whole decoy system, which is a honeypot.

questions.stem: Nandi is evaluating a set of candidate systems to replace a biometric authentication mechanism in her organization. What metric would be the best way to compare the effectiveness of the different systems?
questions.explanation: The false acceptance rate (FAR) is the rate at which the system inadvertently admits an unauthorized user, while the false rejection rate (FRR) is the rate at which the system inadvertently rejects an authorized user. Both the FAR and FRR may be modified by adjusting the sensitivity of the system. The crossover error rate (CER) is the point where both the false acceptance rate and the false rejection rate cross. The CER is less subject to manipulation and is, therefore, the best metric to use for evaluating systems. The FDR is not a metric used to evaluate authentication systems.
optionNotes: Incorrect. FAR is the rate at which unauthorized users are wrongly accepted. Adjusting the system's sensitivity changes it, so comparing FAR values from different systems isn't fair.
Incorrect. FRR is the rate at which authorized users are wrongly rejected. Like FAR, it moves when sensitivity is adjusted, so it isn't a reliable basis for comparing systems.
Correct. CER is the point where FAR and FRR are equal. Sensitivity settings can't easily skew it, which makes it the best single metric for comparing biometric systems.
Incorrect. FDR isn't a metric used to evaluate authentication or biometric systems. It's a distractor.

questions.stem:
Sean suspects that an individual in his company is smuggling out secret information despite his company's careful use of data loss prevention systems. He discovers that the suspect is posting photos, including the one shown here, to public Internet message boards. What type of technique may the individuals be using to hide messages inside this image?
[Figure, described in text: a photograph of both sides of an 1828 gold coin of the Provincias del Rio de la Plata.]
questions.explanation: Steganography is the art of using cryptographic techniques to embed secret messages within other content. Steganographic algorithms work by making invisible alterations to files, such as modifying the least significant bits of the many bits that make up image files. VPNs may be used to obscure secret communications, but they provide protection in transit and can't be used to embed information in an image. Watermarking does embed information in an image but with the intent of protecting intellectual property. A still image would not be used for a covert timing channel because it is a fixed file.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Watermarking does embed information in an image, but its purpose is to protect intellectual property or mark ownership. It isn't used to sneak secret messages out.
Incorrect. A VPN protects data while it's in transit by encrypting the tunnel. It can't embed hidden information inside an image file posted publicly.

Correct. Steganography hides secret messages inside other content by making changes you can't see, such as altering the least significant bits of an image's pixels. That fits photos posted publicly to get data past DLP.
Incorrect. A covert timing channel signals information by changing the timing of events. A still image is a fixed file, so it can't serve as a timing channel.

questions.stem: Roger is concerned that a third-party firm hired to develop code for an internal application will embed a backdoor in the code. The developer retains rights to the intellectual property and will only deliver the software in its final form. Which one of the following languages would be least susceptible to this type of attack because it would provide Roger with code that is human-readable in its final form?
questions.explanation: JavaScript is an interpreted language so the code is not compiled prior to execution, allowing Roger to inspect the contents of the code. C, C++, and Java are all compiled languages—a compiler produces an executable file that is not human-readable.
optionNotes: Correct. JavaScript is interpreted, so it ships as source code and isn't compiled before it runs. Roger can read the delivered code and look for a backdoor.
Incorrect. C is a compiled language. The developer would hand over an executable binary that isn't human-readable, so a backdoor would be hard to spot.
Incorrect. C++ is compiled into machine code. The final product is a non-human-readable executable that Roger can't inspect line by line.
Incorrect. Java is compiled before delivery (to bytecode). The book counts it as compiled, so its final form isn't human-readable source.

questions.stem: Jesse is looking at the /etc/passwd file on a system configured to use shadowed passwords. What should she expect to see in the password field of this file?
questions.explanation: When a system is configured to use shadowed passwords, the /etc/passwd file contains only the character x in the place of a password. It would not contain any passwords, in either plaintext, encrypted, or hashed form.
optionNotes: Incorrect. With shadowing turned on, /etc/passwd holds no passwords at all, so plaintext passwords won't appear there.
Incorrect. No encrypted passwords are kept in /etc/passwd when shadowing is used. The password field only contains a placeholder character.
Incorrect. The password hashes are moved to /etc/shadow, which only root can read. That leaves /etc/passwd with no hash, just a placeholder.
Correct. On a shadowed system, /etc/passwd has just the character x in the password field. The x means the real password hash is stored in /etc/shadow.

questions.stem: Rob recently received a notice from a vendor that the EOL date is approaching for a firewall platform that is used in his organization. What action should Rob take?
options: Prepare to discontinue use of the platform as soon as possible.
Immediately discontinue use of the device.
Prepare to discontinue use of the device as part of the organization's normal planning cycle.
questions.explanation: The end-of-life (EOL) date for a product is normally the date that the vendor will stop selling a product. It is reasonable to continue using the product as long as support remains available. Rob should begin making plans to discontinue use of the product, pending the announcement of an end-of-support (EOS) date.
optionNotes: Incorrect. This overreacts. EOL only means the vendor stops selling the product, and support usually continues for a while. There's no urgency, so replacement can follow the normal planning cycle.

Incorrect. Dropping the device immediately is unnecessary and disruptive. The firewall is still supported after the EOL date, so it's reasonable to keep using it until an end-of-support date approaches.
Correct. EOL means sales stop, but support continues. Rob should plan the replacement through the normal planning cycle while waiting for an end-of-support (EOS) date to be announced.
Incorrect. Doing nothing ignores the coming loss of support. Once EOS arrives, there will be no more patches, so Rob needs to start planning a replacement now.

questions.stem: What principle states that an individual should make every effort to complete their responsibilities in an accurate and timely manner?
questions.explanation: The due care principle states that an individual should react in a situation using the same level of care that would be expected from any reasonable person. It is a very broad standard. The due diligence principle is a more specific component of due care that states that an individual assigned a responsibility should exercise due care to complete it accurately and in a timely manner. Least privilege says that an individual should have the minimum set of permissions necessary to carry out their work. Separation of duties says that no single person should have the right to perform two distinct tasks, which, when combined, constitute a highly privileged action.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Least privilege means giving a person only the minimum permissions their job needs. It covers access rights, not finishing assigned work accurately and on time.

Incorrect. Separation of duties keeps one person from performing two tasks that together make up a highly privileged action. It's a control against fraud and abuse, not a standard for how diligently someone does their work.

Incorrect. Due care is the broad standard of acting the way any reasonable person would. The more specific duty to complete assigned responsibilities accurately and on time is due diligence, which is a component of due care.
Correct. Due diligence is the specific part of due care that requires a person given a responsibility to complete it accurately and on time.

questions.stem: Tony is developing a data classification system for his organization. What factor should he use as the primary driver when determining the classification level of each category of information?
questions.explanation: Information should be classified based upon its sensitivity. This may be due to the value of the information to the organization, the damage caused if lost or compromised, or other factors. The source of the information is one possible contributing factor to the sensitivity level. The likelihood of loss or theft is a component of risk but does not contribute to the classification level.
optionNotes: Correct. Classification levels are driven by sensitivity, meaning the value of the information and how much damage its disclosure, loss or compromise would cause the organization.
Incorrect. Where data came from can add to its sensitivity, but it is only one input. It is not the main factor that sets the classification level.
