[Figure, described in text: a document with three sections: an Executive Summary section with a high-level schedule of key activities and milestones; detailed project tasks for the applicable SDLC phases; and special interest areas tracked outside the SDLC phase areas as required. Each section shows lists of items with task bars.]
questions.explanation: The work breakdown structure (WBS) is an important project management tool that divides the work done for a large project into smaller components. It is not a project plan because it does not describe timing or resources. Test analyses are used during later phases of the development effort to report test results. Functional requirements may be included in a work breakdown structure, but they are not the full WBS.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Functional requirements describe what the software must do. They may show up inside a WBS, but they aren't the whole breakdown of project work by phase shown here.

Correct. A work breakdown structure splits a large project into smaller pieces: an executive summary, detailed tasks for each SDLC phase, and special interest areas. That matches the document described.
Incorrect. A test analysis report records test results in later development phases. It isn't a planning document Norm would get at the start of a project.
Incorrect. A project plan describes timing and assigns resources. A WBS only breaks the work into components, so this document isn't a full project plan.

questions.stem: Kolin is searching for a network security solution that will allow him to help reduce zero-day attacks while using identities to enforce a security policy on systems before they connect to the network. What type of solution should Kolin implement?
questions.explanation: Network Access Control (NAC) systems can be used to authenticate users and then validate their system's compliance with a security standard before they are allowed to connect to the network. Enforcing security profiles can help reduce zero-day attacks, making NAC a useful solution. A firewall can't enforce system security policies, whereas an IDS can only monitor for attacks and alarm when they happen. Thus, neither a firewall nor an IDS meets Kolin's needs. Finally, port security is a MAC address-based security feature that can restrict only which systems or devices can connect to a given port.
optionNotes: Incorrect. A firewall filters traffic based on rules but can't authenticate users or check a system's compliance with security policy before it connects, so it doesn't do what Kolin needs.

Correct. NAC authenticates users and checks that their systems comply with a security standard before they're allowed on the network. Enforcing these security profiles indirectly reduces zero-day attacks.
Incorrect. An IDS only monitors for attacks and raises alarms when they happen. It doesn't use identities or enforce system security policy before devices connect.
Incorrect. Port security works on MAC addresses and only limits which devices can connect to a given switch port. It doesn't use identities or check whether a system complies with policy.

questions.stem: Gwen comes across an application that is running under a service account on a web server. The service account has full administrative rights to the server. What principle of information security does this violate?
questions.explanation: This scenario violates the least privilege principle because an application should never require full administrative rights to run. Gwen should update the service account to have only the privileges necessary to support the application.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Need to know limits access to specific data or information that a person needs for their work. The issue in this question is too many system rights given to a service account, not access to classified information.

Incorrect. Separation of duties divides sensitive tasks among different people so no single person controls a whole process. Here one application account simply has more rights than it needs, so no task is being split.
Correct. An application should never need full administrative rights to run. Least privilege means the service account should have only the privileges required to support the application.
Incorrect. Job rotation regularly moves staff between roles so fraud is easier to detect. It does not apply to how many privileges a service account has.

questions.stem: Ed is developing a set of key performance and risk indicators for his organization's information security program. Which of the following are commonly used indicators? (Select all that apply.)
options: Number of malicious site visit attempts
questions.explanation: Organizations typically use the time to resolve vulnerabilities, the number of account compromises, and the number of attempts by users to visit malicious sites as indicators. The number of scheduled audits is not normally a measure of the performance of an information security team. A more appropriate indicator in this area is the number of repeat audit findings.
optionNotes: Incorrect. How many audits are scheduled says nothing about how well the security team performs. A better indicator in this area is the number of repeat audit findings.
Correct. Time to resolve vulnerabilities is a common KPI because it shows how quickly the security program finds and fixes weaknesses.
Correct. Counting how often users try to visit malicious sites is a common risk indicator. It shows user behavior and how well web filtering and awareness training are working.
Correct. The number of account compromises is a common indicator because it directly measures security incidents that actually affected the organization.

questions.stem: Kara is documenting the results of a vulnerability scan. After reviewing one finding, she determined that the vulnerability did exist. The team then implemented a configuration change that corrected the issue. How should Kara classify this vulnerability in her report?
questions.explanation: This is a true positive report because the scan detected the vulnerability, and the vulnerability actually existed. The fact that the team later remediated the vulnerability could be noted in the report, but it does not change the result of the scan or its classification. True negatives occur when scans correctly note the absence of a vulnerability. False positives occur when scans report the presence of a vulnerability that does not actually exist. False negatives occur when scans report that no vulnerability exists when one does, in fact, exist.
optionNotes: Correct. The scan flagged the vulnerability and Kara confirmed it actually existed, so it's a true positive. The later fix can go in the report, but it doesn't change how the scan result is classified.
Incorrect. A true negative is when the scan correctly reports that no vulnerability is present. Here the scan reported a vulnerability, and it was real.
Incorrect. A false positive is when the scan reports a vulnerability that doesn't actually exist. Kara confirmed this one did exist, and remediating it afterward doesn't make the finding false.
Incorrect. A false negative is when the scan misses a vulnerability that really exists. In this case the scan did detect the vulnerability.

Why does Nikto flag the /test directory?

Test directories often contain scripts that can be misused.

Incorrect. Test directories aren't normally used to store sensitive data. Nikto flags /test/ for the leftover scripts or test content it may hold, not because it's a known data store.
Correct. Test directories often hold scripts with weak protections, or other leftover data an attacker can misuse. That's why Nikto reports /test/ as 'This might be interesting...'
Incorrect. Having a test directory isn't a common indicator of compromise. Nikto is flagging possible exposure and misconfiguration, not evidence of an intrusion.

Why does Nikto identify directory indexing as an issue?
options: It lists files in a directory.
Directory indexing can result in a denial-of-service attack.
Directory indexing is off by default, potentially indicating compromise.
questions.explanation: Directory indexing may not initially seem like an issue during a penetration test, but simply knowing the name and location of files can provide an attacker with quite a bit of information about an organization, as well as a list of potentially accessible files. XDRF is not a type of attack, and indexing is not a denial-of-service attack vector. Directory indexing being turned on is typically either due to design or because the server was misconfigured at setup, rather than being a sign of attack.
optionNotes: Correct. When directory indexing is on, the server lists the files in a directory. That shows an attacker file names and locations, maps the site, and can reveal sensitive files they might be able to open.

Incorrect. XDRF is not a real attack type. It may be a mix-up with XSRF/CSRF, which is unrelated to directory indexing. Also, the XST finding in the output comes from the TRACE method, not from indexing.
Incorrect. Directory indexing does not lead to denial of service. It is an information-disclosure problem: it exposes file listings but does not exhaust the server's resources.

Incorrect. Indexing is usually turned on by design or left on through a setup misconfiguration. It is not a sign of compromise, and Nikto flags it because it exposes information, not because it suggests an attack.

Nikto lists OSVDB-877, noting that the system may be vulnerable to XST. What would this type of attack allow an attacker to do?
questions.explanation: Cross-site tracing (XST) leverages the HTTP TRACE or TRACK methods and could be used to steal a user's cookies via cross-site scripting (XSS). The other options are not industry terms for web application or web server attacks or vulnerabilities.
optionNotes: Incorrect. "Cross-site targeting" isn't a real attack term. XST stands for cross-site tracing, which abuses the HTTP TRACE/TRACK methods. It doesn't describe targeting sites in general.

Correct. Cross-site tracing uses the HTTP TRACE or TRACK method, usually together with XSS. TRACE echoes the request back, so it can expose a user's cookies, including HttpOnly ones, and an attacker can steal them.
Incorrect. "Countering SQL tracing" isn't an industry term. XST abuses HTTP TRACE on the web server and has nothing to do with SQL or database tracing. SQL attacks would be SQL injection.
Incorrect. XST doesn't modify any "TRACE information." It abuses the TRACE method's echo behavior to read sensitive headers such as cookies. "Modifying TRACE information" isn't a recognized attack.

questions.stem: Who would be the most appropriate supervisor for an organization's chief audit executive (CAE)?
questions.explanation: The chief audit executive (CAE) should report to the most senior possible leader to avoid conflicts of interest. Of the choices provided, the chief executive officer (CEO) is the most senior position and the best option. It is also possible to provide an added degree of independence by having the CAE report to the board of directors, either as a primary reporting line or as a dotted line relationship.
optionNotes: Incorrect. The CIO runs IT operations, and internal audit regularly reviews those operations. Having the CAE report to the CIO would create a conflict of interest, and the CIO is not the most senior leader available.

Incorrect. The CISO's security program is itself something internal audit reviews. The CISO also typically reports to senior management, so placing the CAE under the CISO would undermine audit independence.

Correct. The CAE should report to the most senior leader possible to avoid conflicts of interest. Of these choices, the CEO is the most senior. A primary or dotted-line report to the board adds further independence.
Incorrect. The CFO owns the financial processes and controls that internal audit examines, so reporting to the CFO creates a conflict of interest. The CFO also ranks below the CEO.

questions.stem: Ursula believes that many individuals in her organization are storing sensitive information on their laptops in a manner that is unsafe and potentially violates the organization's security policy. What control can she use to identify the presence of these files?
questions.explanation: Data loss prevention (DLP) systems specialize in the identification of sensitive information. In this case, Ursula would like to identify the presence of this information on endpoint devices, so she should choose an endpoint DLP control. Network-based DLP would not detect stored information unless the user transmits it over the network. Intrusion prevention systems (IPSs) are designed to detect and block attacks in progress, not necessarily the presence of sensitive information.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Network DLP only inspects data as it moves across the network. It won't see files sitting on a laptop unless the user transmits them.
Incorrect. A network IPS detects and blocks attacks in transit. It isn't built to find sensitive content, and it can't see data stored on laptops.
Correct. DLP is designed to identify sensitive information, and an endpoint DLP agent scans the files stored on the laptop itself, so it can find the data at rest that Ursula is worried about.
Incorrect. An endpoint IPS detects and blocks attacks in progress on a host. It doesn't scan stored files for sensitive content, which is the job of DLP content discovery.

questions.stem: In what cloud computing model does the customer build a cloud computing environment in their own data center or build an environment in another data center that is for the customer's exclusive use?
questions.explanation: In the private cloud computing model, the cloud computing environment is dedicated to a single organization and does not follow the shared tenancy model. The environment may be built by the company in its own data center or built by a vendor at a co-location site.
optionNotes: Incorrect. A public cloud is open to many customers at once. They share the provider's infrastructure, so it is not built in the customer's own data center or reserved for one customer.
Correct. A private cloud serves only one organization and has no shared tenancy. It can be built in the company's own data center or by a vendor at a co-location site.
Incorrect. A hybrid cloud combines private and public cloud resources. Because it includes shared public infrastructure, it does not match an environment reserved only for the customer.
Incorrect. 'Shared cloud' is not a standard deployment model. Even taken literally, it means several tenants use the same environment, which is the opposite of exclusive use.

questions.stem: Which one of the following technologies is designed to prevent a web server going offline from becoming a single point of failure in a web application architecture?
questions.explanation: Load balancing helps to ensure that a failed server will not take a website or service offline. Dual power supplies only work to prevent failure of a power supply or power source. IPS can help to prevent attacks, and RAID can help prevent a disk failure from taking a system offline.
optionNotes: Correct. Load balancing spreads requests across several web servers, so if one fails the others keep serving traffic. The site stays online and the single server is no longer a single point of failure.
Incorrect. Dual power supplies only protect against a failed power supply or power source. If the server itself fails or goes offline, the web service still goes down.
Incorrect. An intrusion prevention system detects and blocks attacks. It is a security control, not a redundancy mechanism, so it can't keep the service running when a server goes offline.
Incorrect. RAID gives disk-level redundancy, so one failed drive doesn't take the system offline. It doesn't help when the whole web server fails.

questions.stem: Alice wants to send Bob a message with the confidence that Bob will know the message was not altered while in transit. What security goal is Alice trying to achieve?
questions.explanation: Integrity ensures that unauthorized changes are not made to data while stored or in transit.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Confidentiality keeps a message from being read by unauthorized parties, usually through encryption. Alice wants Bob to know the message wasn't changed, not that nobody else could read it.

Incorrect. Nonrepudiation stops the sender (or recipient) from denying they took part, for example by using a digital signature. It is about proving who sent the message, not about catching changes made in transit.
Incorrect. Authentication proves who sent the message, so Bob would know it came from Alice. It does not show on its own that the content arrived unaltered.
Correct. Integrity ensures no unauthorized changes are made to data while it is stored or in transit, which is exactly what Alice wants Bob to be sure of.

questions.stem:
What network topology is shown here?
[Figure, described in text: five workstations and a server, each connected by its own cable to a single central device.]
questions.explanation: A star topology uses a central connection device. Ethernet networks may look like a star, but they are actually a logical bus topology that is sometimes deployed in a physical star.
optionNotes: Incorrect. In a ring, devices are linked one to the next in a closed loop. The figure has no loop: every node has its own cable to one central device.

Incorrect. A bus connects every device to one shared backbone cable that needs termination at both ends. The book notes that Ethernet is a logical bus, but the physical layout shown, with a central device, is a star.
Correct. A star topology uses a central connection device, such as a hub or switch, and each system connects to it over its own dedicated segment. That is exactly what the figure shows.
Incorrect. A mesh links devices directly to many or all other devices for redundancy. Here each node has a single link, and only to the central device.

questions.stem: Monica is developing a software application that calculates an individual's body mass index for use in medical planning. She would like to include a control on the field where the physician enters an individual's weight to ensure that the weight falls within an expected range. What type of control should Monica use?
questions.explanation: Input validation ensures that the data provided to a program as input matches the expected parameters. Limit checks are a special form of input validation that ensure that the value remains within an expected range, as is the case described in this scenario. Fail open and fail secure are options when planning for possible system failures. Buffer bounds are not a type of software control.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Fail open describes how a system behaves when it fails, defaulting to allowing access. It's part of planning for failures and doesn't validate whether an input value falls in a range.

Incorrect. Fail secure is a failure-handling choice where the system defaults to a locked or denied state. It deals with system failures, not with checking that a weight entry is within expected bounds.
Correct. A limit check is a form of input validation that makes sure a value, here a patient's weight, falls inside an expected range before the program accepts it.
Incorrect. Buffer bounds is not a type of software control, so it can't be the control used to confirm that an entered weight falls within an expected range.

questions.stem:
Match the following numbered types of testing methodologies with the lettered correct level of knowledge:
